title: Ship the Degraded Brief
scenario: It is 6:52 AM on the quarantine morning. The brief ships at 7:00 with a hub missing, a late feed on the record, and no approval - because nothing escalated under the ratified policy. Shipping degraded output well is a designed skill: the brief must carry its incident, label its gaps, and explain why no one signed it.
input: Assembly rule for degraded runs: the brief renders from stored artifacts only, and adds an Incidents section sourced from the feed incident record. The headline comes from risk-evaluation.json (highest surviving classification). The approval line must state WHY no approval exists: no hub reached the escalation band of the ratified policy. The brief is explicitly marked degraded.
instructions: Open the incident record and the risk record on the shelf.
Fill the headline from the highest surviving classification.
Fill the Incidents section from the incident record: timings, quarantined hub, brief mode.
Fill the policy version the no-approval line cites.

shelf.producedBy: Handle the Morning the Feed Breaks

validation.template:
# Meridian Morning Market Brief - degraded run
Status: released without approval - no hub reached the escalation band of policy v{{policyVersion}}

## Headline
{{headlineHub}} moved {{headlineMovePct}} percent day-over-day - {{headlineStatus}} under the ratified thresholds.

## Hub Summary
ERCOT peak 198, settled 149. MISO peak 81, settled 76.

## Incidents
Feed expected {{feedExpectedAt}}, arrived {{feedArrivedAt}}. {{quarantinedHub}} row quarantined (malformed) - values withheld, vendor notified.
This brief is marked {{briefMode}}: today's numbers are partial by design.
Prepared by the Meridian workflow at 6:52 AM.

slots.hint: The highest surviving classification in risk-evaluation.json.

slots.hint: Its status in risk-evaluation.json - note that it did NOT escalate.

copilotPrompt: Assemble a degraded brief from stored artifacts: the ratified policy version, the highest surviving classification (hub, move, status) from the risk record, and the Incidents facts (expected/arrived times, quarantined hub, brief mode) from the feed incident record. The status line explains why no approval exists.
successMessage: Degraded brief rendered. It ships on time, tells the whole truth, and explains its own missing signature.

intro.heading: Before you assemble: shipping degraded is a skill

sections.title: The brief carries its incident
sections.body: On a normal morning the incident record would live in a log nobody reads. Degraded-mode design puts it IN the deliverable: the reader learns about the late feed and the quarantined hub in the same glance as the prices.

sections.title: Explain the missing signature
sections.body: A brief with no approval line invites the worst assumption. This one states the reason: nothing reached the ratified escalation band. An absent control, explained, is a working system; an absent control, unexplained, is a finding.

sections.title: The whole hard tier converges here
sections.body: The incident record (feed failure), the degraded classifications (quarantine), and the ratified thresholds (your redesign) all meet in this one document. Assembly on a bad morning is where design quality becomes visible.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd assemble the final brief by dropping the cleaned numbers and the risk verdicts into the template, ready to send at 7:00.

tools.powerAutomate: 'Create HTML table' + 'Compose' to build the body, then 'Send an email'
tools.zapier: a 'Formatter' build step feeding 'Send Outbound Email' / Gmail
tools.python: render the template with the day data, output HTML or markdown

takeaway.heading: Degraded brief shipped
points: You shipped on time with partial data - and the document itself says which parts are partial and why.
The missing approval is explained by rule, not left as an ominous blank.
Incident facts flowed from the incident record into the deliverable: failures surface where readers actually look.
This is the last mile of resilience: detection, quarantine, honest classification, and now honest publication.
The workflow can now deliver trustworthy output on exactly the mornings that used to produce either silence or fiction.
